# Common declaration/pattern checking: informed first-source context

Prepared before the first invocation. This is an informed development study,
not a blind model benchmark. Codex authored the programs after reading the
current common AST, scanner/parser, source collection, finite/sized profile
contracts, exact pattern and ownership Reference, selected CLI grammar and
earlier authoring records. The deployed model identifier/sampling settings are
not available; no external model was invoked.

The parent reports local, unpushed source-collection commit
`b544cd2d96dcc94e0ef29b28e6b08979bca5d9b1` and a successful actual Rust
1.85.0 validation. This study reuses the already built fixed CLI at
`/private/tmp/qleisli-bounded-validation-target/debug/qleisli`; it does not
build or attest that binary from this commit. Exact CLI/native, current Rust
and native source, stdlib/manifest, Cargo and constitutional contract hashes
are captured before/after every sequence. Byte identity is not build
attestation, proof, authorship authentication or release approval.

Eight complete original projects use current grammar: nested runtime tuple
parameters retaining ordinary Unit, duplicate runtime parameter names,
consume-before-rebind with h, hiding a live owner, join(q,q), quantum wildcard
Q<Unit>, quantum wildcard Q<Bits<0>>, and a never-called invalid sibling. Their
intended source obligations are described independently in prerequisites.md,
without predicting which current checking/profile rule is reached.

Each project declares schema-2 edition 2026. All study-defined interfaces use
at most two physical qubits. The finite public path still checks all existing
embedded library declarations, including its pre-existing four-bit library
body; no new large case is generated or executed. No run/sample command,
maximum-size test, Cargo build or Lean build is part of this study.

For each unchanged source, capture finite project check text/JSON and selected
explicit-module auto-profile check text/JSON. Capture selected emit-proposal
JSON as an untrusted producer result; emission invokes no native acceptance.
A transparent argument-logging launcher delegates to the same pinned native
binary. Actual native calls, exact diagnostics and proposal bytes are retained.
Selected checks have complete supplied-declaration source scope, while native
checking concerns only the selected concrete instance. Finite traversal and
native-producer/request scope remain separate from general source preservation.

Preserve real unsupported/profile errors rather than assuming equivalence.
In particular finite register-type rejection may mask the intended
Q<Bits<0>> wildcard ownership obligation; that rejection does not establish
its later ownership rule. A successful check/proposal is not an independent
functional or arbitrary-reference oracle. No source repair is planned; if one
is needed it must use a separate complete attempt with its actual reason.

Adopted QS-2026-01, PR-2026-01, RS-2026-01 and EXACT-2026-01 apply. Both admitted
ordinary QLV1 structural guarantees retain their exact scopes/premises and
pending broader obligations. The study creates no new constitutional
interpretation, primitive, acceptance rule, guarantee or common checker
completion. GitHub remains the work tracker; this is first-source evidence,
not another backlog.
